clue.text: Mark with spots led astray installing smartphone program

indicators.note: installing means the shuffled letters take the program in among them
led astray means the letters of 'led' wander out of their order

parts.note: an app is a program for a smartphone

explanation.surface: A rogue phone app sends someone off course, as if it had been sneaked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led astray' reads as being misled, but 'astray' is the anagram signal, giving DLE, which 'installing' wraps round the phone app.
explanation.definitionFit: To dapple is to cover with small patches or flecks of colour, which is a verb for spotting.

clue.text: Plant used for colour, as a Welshman would say

indicators.note: as pairs with 'say' to frame the words as something spoken
say tells us the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: Dai is the stock Welsh man's name in crosswords; taken as the word would

explanation.surface: A plant is used to dye cloth, and its name is offered as a Welsh speaker would pronounce something.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'Dai would' gives the plant's name; Dai (short for David) is the standard crossword Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyewood is any tree whose timber yields a dye, such as logwood, so it is a plant used for colouring.

clue.text: To the audience, type of TV view material

indicators.note: to the audience means as heard by listeners, so we want a word sounding like another

parts.note: pay-per-view is a type of TV; before 'view' come the words PAY PER

explanation.surface: An audience is offered a kind of television viewing material.
explanation.walkthrough: Pay-per-view television charges per programme; 'pay per', said aloud, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper is a material used for writing, wrapping and printing.

clue.text: Rugby players upend that man over tense tradesman

parts.note: locks are forwards in the second row of a rugby scrum

indicators.note: over here means covering or around, so the turned word goes round the tense letter
upend in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, so read from bottom up

parts.note: that man means him
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Rugby forwards flip a man over in a scrum, in a tense moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upend' turns HIM to MIH, and 'over' puts it round T to give MITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith is a craftsman who makes and repairs locks, one kind of tradesman.

clue.text: They protect the Crown

parts.note: the crown is also the top of the head, which this headgear guards

explanation.surface: Royal guards protect the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Crown' suggests the monarchy and its guards; read literally it is the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Protective headgear covers the top of the skull, which is also called the crown.

clue.text: Negotiated hard deal about riding horse

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: riding means the horse sits inside the rearranged letters
about means the letters of 'deal' are moved around

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A tough deal was struck over a horse being ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiated hard' looks like the whole definition, but 'hard' is H. 'about' rearranges the deal into ALED, and 'riding' seats the horse inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to bargain over a price, so a past-tense verb meaning bargained or negotiated.

clue.text: Transport gold in two hands by end of day

indicators.note: in means the gold sits inside the two hands

parts.note: left and right hands, L and R
or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of 'day'

explanation.surface: Gold is moved by hand before the day is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry is a British truck, a vehicle of transport.

clue.text: Illustrated River Dee, clear down the middle

indicators.note: down the middle means the clear word runs inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
clear means plain
dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

explanation.surface: Someone illustrates the River Dee, clear right down its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Dee' is not the Welsh river: it is EXE then the letter dee.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate a point is to make it clear, so explained matches illustrated.

clue.text: Climbing mountains with peaks of snow hurts a little

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: the Alps are mountains

indicators.note: peaks of means the tops, the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Climbing snowy peaks hurts a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns ALPS into SPLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash of milk is a small amount, so a splash means a little.

clue.text: 1 of 2 or 1 in 3, roughly?

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are put together loosely, out of order

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
three spelt out

explanation.surface: A puzzle about fractions: one of two, or about one in three?
explanation.walkthrough: The digits look like a probability question, but 1 is the numeral I and 3 is THREE, which 'roughly' shuffles together.
explanation.definitionFit: Either picks one of two possibilities, as in 'either road'.

clue.text: Old setter's good with child

parts.note: ex means former or old
pectin is what makes jam set

explanation.surface: An old crossword setter is good with children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is not the compiler but pectin, the setting agent in jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is an idiom for pregnant, which is also what 'with child' means.

clue.text: Reject outcast swapping sides

indicators.note: swapping sides means the word's left and right are exchanged, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a leper is a social outcast

explanation.surface: An outcast is rejected and switches allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back or rebuff, a verb meaning to reject.

clue.text: Monsters finally go looking for three knights

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Monsters at last go hunting for three knights.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, a kind of monster.

clue.text: According to Spooner, Murs trick with soap?

indicators.note: Spooner means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: Olly Murs is a British pop singer
a hoax is a trick

explanation.surface: A pop singer plays a trick involving soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olly hoax' with its opening sounds swapped becomes the answer; Olly has no opening consonant, so the H simply moves across. Hollyoaks is a long-running British TV soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollyoaks is a British television soap opera, an example of a soap.

clue.text: Record rise in disorder after parties

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the parties

parts.note: a do is a party, so dos are parties

indicators.note: in disorder means the letters of 'rise' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Records show a rise in rowdiness after parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents about a person or subject, a record.

clue.text: Weak bowling technique Cook sees, getting over 50

parts.note: spin is a style of bowling in cricket

indicators.note: getting over means the cooked letters cover the fifty
cook means the letters are cooked up into a new order

parts.note: L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: Alastair Cook watches spin bowling as he passes fifty runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' turns SEES into ESES, and 'getting over' puts it round L for ELESS. Alastair Cook was an England batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Spineless means lacking backbone or courage, so feeble or weak.

clue.text: Courting daughter with giant fiddle

indicators.note: fiddle means the letters are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter is courted by a giant playing the fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dating is going out romantically with someone, as courting once meant.

clue.text: A number score twice with only headers

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: headers means the heads, the first letters of the neighbouring words

explanation.surface: A footballer scores twice, using only headers.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-two is a whole number, so it is one example of a number.

clue.text: Struggles with 5 + 8 + 7? I've left 'e' out, not even in order

indicators.note: left means the letters of I've go away from the first number

parts.note: five spelt out
I've, without its apostrophe, is the letters IVE

indicators.note: out means the letter e is removed from the second number

parts.note: eight spelt out

indicators.note: not means the word even is subtracted from the third number

parts.note: seven spelt out
the word even itself

explanation.surface: A puzzling arithmetic sum, with letters being dropped in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 + 8 + 7' are the words FIVE, EIGHT, SEVEN, not answers elsewhere. 'I've left' leaves F, ''e' out' leaves IGHT, and 'not even' leaves S; 'in order' says the steps go to the numbers in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Fights are physical or verbal struggles, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Smartens up princess, scruffy without pin

indicators.note: scruffy means the letters are messed up into a new order
without means the letters of pin are left out of the mixture

explanation.surface: A princess tidies herself up, looking scruffy without her brooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smartens up' looks like the whole definition, but 'up' is fodder: UP PRINCESS minus P, I, N, shuffled, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce something is to make it neat and trim, a verb for smartening.

clue.text: Turn provided by senior cricketer

indicators.note: turn means the word for provided is turned round

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'
an elder is someone senior

explanation.surface: An older cricketer takes his turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder is a cricketer on the fielding side who stops and catches the ball.

clue.text: Stronger sack carrying money (roubles)

indicators.note: carrying means the sack word holds the money letter inside

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
R is the abbreviation for roubles

explanation.surface: A stronger sack is needed for carrying the money, in roubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmer means more solid or steady, a comparative close to stronger.

clue.text: Finds another role for exceptional actress

indicators.note: exceptional suggests the letters are taken out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An exceptional actress is given a new part.
explanation.definitionFit: To recast a part is to give an actor a different role in a production.

clue.text: Pieces of meat, drink and cocktail during the weekend?

indicators.note: during means the drink and tail letter come inside the weekend letters

parts.note: Saturday and Sunday each begin with S
tea is a drink
read as cock's tail, the last letter of cock

explanation.surface: Weekend plans: steak, a drink and a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' is not a drink: it is the tail of 'cock', K.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaks are thick slices of beef or other meat.

clue.text: City official tracking the movement of Sterling?

definitions.text: City official tracking the movement of Sterling?

parts.words: City official tracking the movement of Sterling?
parts.note: a city's financial officer keeps track of where its pounds sterling go

explanation.surface: A City of London figure watches the pound move on the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterling suggests the currency markets of the City; the officer in question simply looks after an organisation's money.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the official in charge of an organisation's or council's funds.

clue.text: Black market stocks book

indicators.note: stocks means holds inside, so the market word contains the book letter

parts.note: a sale is a market

explanation.surface: A black market deals in books.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black.

clue.text: Matter of time before corrupt cop jails international

indicators.note: before means time comes first
jails means the rearranged letters lock up the international letter
corrupt means the letters of cop are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: It's a matter of time before a bent policeman locks up a foreign criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' makes OPC from COP, and 'jails' puts I inside: OPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject under discussion, one sense of matter.

clue.text: Delivering fruit precisely

indicators.note: delivering, as in delivering a speech, means saying aloud

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: Fruit is delivered with precision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivering' is not carrying goods but uttering, so the fruit's name is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb as an adverb means exactly, as in 'plumb in the middle'.

clue.text: One empty beer returned for bitter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: returned means the remaining letters are sent back the other way
empty means remove the inside, keeping just the outer letters of beer

explanation.surface: Someone takes back an empty beer glass for a bitter, a British pale ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves BR, and 'returned' turns it to RB. Bitter is a British ale, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare word for sour or harsh in taste, the same as bitter.

clue.text: Cliches etc thus translated to cover new section

indicators.note: to cover means the jumbled letters surround the new letter
translated means the letters are turned into a new form

explanation.surface: Tired phrases, et cetera, are translated for a new section of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' turns ETC THUS into CHESTUT, which 'to cover' puts round N.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a stale joke or story, so chestnuts are worn-out cliches.

clue.text: Troy besieged by messy rebels with special structures

indicators.note: besieged by means Troy's letter is surrounded by the others
rebels means the letters revolt against their order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for troy weight

explanation.surface: Troy is besieged by an unruly rebel army with special siege structures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' turns MESSY into SYSEM, which 'besieged by' wraps round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems are organised sets of parts, which is a sense of structures.

clue.text: Top of double-decker bus to crash into reservations

indicators.note: top of means take the first letter of double-decker
crash means the letters smash into a new order

explanation.surface: The top deck of a London bus crashes into something, raising doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' turns BUS TO into OUBTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubts are misgivings, which is also what reservations means.
